title: Directed Action Proposal
description: A machine-readable proposal for a single AWS DevOps Agent directed action, derived from a read-only recommendation record. It names the exact mutating operation, its parameters, the guardrail evaluation, and the approval scope. A directed action is never executed without per-action operator approval in chat; this record describes what would be approved and executed. One directed action corresponds to one approvable operation on one resource.

id.description: Stable identifier for this directed action proposal.

derivedFromRecommendationId.description: The id of the recommendation record (recommendation.schema.json) this directed action implements. Links the write-path action back to the read-only finding that justified it.

target.description: The single resource the directed action mutates.

service.description: AWS service namespace, for example ec2, s3, cloudwatch, dynamodb.

resourceId.description: Resource identifier or ARN. Referenced by identifier; never embed secrets.

accountId.description: Account identifier. HIGH sensitivity; may be masked in stored output.

operation.description: The exact API operation the agent would invoke via use_aws.

api.description: The mutating API operation in service:Action form, for example ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress or cloudwatch:PutMetricAlarm.

mutating.description: Always true for a directed action. Read-only operations are not directed actions and do not use this schema.

parameters.description: The concrete parameters the operation would be called with. Values must be specific (a named CIDR, a specific retention in days), never wildcards or blanket grants.

guardrailStatus.description: Evaluation of the operation against the agent's service-side guardrails and this repository's prohibited actions.

decision.description: allowed means the operation passes all guardrails. The refused-* values name the specific guardrail that blocks it; a refused action must not be proposed for execution and remains a manual step.

prohibitedActionCheck.description: Result of checking the operation against the SECURITY.md prohibited actions list (no wildcard IAM, no disabling Block Public Access, no 0.0.0.0/0 inbound, no disabling logging or encryption, and so on). failed forces decision to refused-prohibited-action.

requiresPassRole.description: True if the operation would pass an IAM role to a service. Such operations are refused by the agent by default.

deleteClass.description: True if the operation deletes a resource. Delete-class operations are always refused by the agent.

safetyRating.description: Directed actions are state-changing, so they are never GREEN. YELLOW is recoverable; RED is hard to reverse. RED actions require senior approval and are rare because delete-class is already refused.

reversible.description: Whether the change can be reverted with the documented rollback.

escalationRequired.description: Whether the change meets an escalation condition in SECURITY.md (IAM in production, security controls, KMS key policy, aws-auth, SCP, CloudTrail, encryption, or blast radius beyond one account or region).

blastRadius.description: Scope of impact if executed. Cross-account or cross-region actions require additional explicit approval.

approval.description: How the operator approval must be scoped. Every directed action requires approval; this describes the expected finalized scope.

required.description: Always true. AWS DevOps Agent never executes a mutating operation without approval.

scope.description: single-use consumes the approval once. time-window allows reuse for a bounded period (up to 4 hours). One-time changes should be single-use.

ttlSeconds.description: For time-window scope, the reuse window in seconds (maximum 14400 = 4 hours). Omit for single-use.

argumentPins.description: The parameters that must be pinned in the approval so it cannot be widened, for example operation and resource_arn. The finalized scope can narrow but never widen the request.

verification.description: The read-only check to run after execution to confirm the change took effect and had the intended result, for example re-describe the security group and confirm the 0.0.0.0/0 rule is gone.

rollback.description: Explicit steps to revert the change if it makes things worse. Required for every directed action because all directed actions are state-changing.

notes.description: Optional caveats, assumptions, or operator guidance for the approval decision.
